 WMU, Columbus Families Encouraged to Attend FAFSA Informational Sessions This Evening 
 Posted By: Brendan Schnoebelen 
 October 29, 2026 @ 6:20 am
 Today's Local News 
 Tweet 
 Share 
 Email 
 The Free Application for Federal Student Aid, commonly known as FAFSA, has opened for the 2027-2028 school year. Staff with the Winfield-Mount Union and Columbus Community School Districts are lending families a helping hand in completing their forms with FAFSA informational nights. 
 Winfield-Mount Union Secondary Principal Gaige Gill explains how the night will work for attendees at WMU, and the benefits of filling out the application, “Basically people just come in when they can, and then an expert kind of grabs them and they just have a conversation. They walk through the process. Basically, they go through it all and they start actually filling it out, and by the time you leave, it’s either complete or it’s very close to being complete. It doesn’t hurt anything to fill out that FAFSA, and it’s kind of a complicated thing. The people that do it walk away so relieved because someone kind of held their hand, walked through it with them, and it’s been a very positive thing.” 
 Gill also added that filling out a FAFSA application opens the door for students to receive grants, scholarships, and other financial aid after graduating high school. 
 Both events are open to all students and families of each district, but are most helpful to seniors and their parents. Those planning to attend the events are asked to bring their 2025 tax information and create their FSA ID if possible before sitting down with an expert. 
 Doors open at both high schools at 4 p.m., ending at 7:30 for WMU and 8 for Columbus.
